item.title: YPP urges NASS to suspend Tinubu’s $20.5bn loan
item.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), Architect Peter Agada, has urged the National Assembly to suspend consideration of President Bola Tinubu’s latest external borrowing request until after the 2027 general elections. Agada made the call in Abuja on Wednesday in reaction to Tinubu’s letter to Senate President Godswill Akpabio seeking approval for $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion in supplementary external borrowing for 2026 and 2027. He said the timing of the request, less than 110 days before the elections, raised concerns, particularly with Nigeria’s public debt standing at ₦166.79 trillion as of June 2026. “Now we want to add another $21.7bn — less than 110 days to the 2027 general election. “For three years, the Federal Government has been unable to fully finance its budget. Capital performance is below 40 per cent. “Contractors are being owed. Yet we are borrowing more. In architecture, you don’t borrow to build a new house when you have not roofed the old one,” he said. The YPP candidate questioned why the government continued to seek substantial loans despite the removal of the petrol subsidy and the floating of the naira, which he said had significantly increased government revenue. “Where did the subsidy savings go? This is the question Emir Sanusi and other leaders have been asking,” he said. Agada also questioned what tangible results the proposed borrowing could deliver within the remaining period before the elections, given the time required to implement major infrastructure projects. “If you approve $20.5bn today, can you complete any power, transport, health or education project in 100 days? No. So what will this money actually do? Pay contractors who are party financiers? Fund election logistics?” he asked. He urged lawmakers to include a clause prohibiting disbursement of the loan proceeds between January and May 2027 if the request was approved. “If you must approve this loan, insert a clear clause: No disbursement from January 2027 to May 2027. The money should come after the election, to whoever wins, not before to the incumbent. That is how you prove it is not political,” he said. Agada argued that the borrowing request could send conflicting signals to investors, given the government’s promotion of its economic reforms and reported endorsements from international development institutions. He proposed alternative ways of financing infrastructure without resorting to additional borrowing, claiming that Nigeria could save more than ₦13 trillion annually through leaner governance without reducing Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) distributions or introducing new taxes. His proposals included cutting the cost of governance by 40 per cent, merging 250 agencies he described as duplicative into 40, and eliminating duplicate vehicle fleets and official trips, which he said could save more than ₦4 trillion. item.title: ‘I can take bullet for him’ — Uba Sani vows to support Tinubu till last minute
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, has declared his readiness to defend President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, saying he can take a bullet for the President and will support him until the last minute. Sani said his support was informed by the benefits Kaduna State had received under the Tinubu administration, including federal appointments, infrastructure projects and funding for transportation and education. Speaking in an interview with Trust TV’s Daily Politics , the governor said his loyalty to Tinubu was driven by the interests of Kaduna State rather than personal favours. Asked whether he could take a political bullet for Tinubu, Sani replied, “I can take it.” He added: “I have no apology for supporting President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and I will continue to support him till last minute and I will tell you why, because many people do not know President Tinubu, I know him, and I’ve been with him for 32 years and I cannot pretend.” According to the governor, Tinubu’s support had helped Kaduna secure key federal appointments and major development projects. Sani cited the appointment of three Kaduna indigenes to strategic federal positions: Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd.); Minister of Environment, Balarabe Abbas Lawal; and Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko. He said he had engaged the President on the appointments, which he described as important to the state’s representation in the Federal Government. “The minister of defence is from Kaduna, Christopher Musa, and I was instrumental in getting him the portfolio. The minister of environment, Balarabe Abbas, is from Kaduna, and recently, when the ministry of sports was collapsed into the national sports commission, Shehu Dikko is from Kaduna,” he said. “Now we have three ministers, and I was instrumental in talking to Mr President. What do I need more than this?” On education, Sani said he had initially requested two additional federal universities for Kaduna, but Tinubu approved four university initiatives. They include the Federal University of Applied Sciences in Kachia, the Federal University of Education in Zaria, the Umaru Musa Yar’Adua University of Petroleum Resources in Rigachikun, and a proposed conversion of Kaduna Polytechnic into a federal university of technology. The governor also credited Tinubu with facilitating funding for the 123-kilometre Kaduna-Birnin Gwari road, which he said had been abandoned for 45 years. He said the President had promised to reconstruct the road during a campaign visit to Kaduna in 2022. Sani said he later reminded Tinubu of the pledge by showing him a video of the commitment, after which N178 billion was released for the project. He added that funding had also been approved for the reconstruction of the road linking Jama’a, Kwoi and Jere, which he said had been in poor condition for nearly four decades. Sani further said Tinubu approved funding for a proposed light rail project in Kadun

item.title: Barau faults Osinbajo’s gloomy assessment of Nigeria’s economy, democracy
item.description: By Henry Umoru, Abuja The Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, APC, Kano North has taken a swipe at former Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo over the gloomy picture he painted of Nigeria’s economy and democratic governance. Senator Barau Jibrin, who noted that Osinbajo got it wrong, said that the administration of President Bola Tinubu is taking steps to address what he described as longstanding challenges confronting the country. According to Jibrin, while Osinbajo’s concerns, particularly those drawn from Afrobarometer surveys on Nigeria and other African countries, were valid, the government needs to improve communication with the people to highlight ongoing efforts to address the challenges. The Deputy President of the Senate made the remarks in Yola, Adamawa State, during a public lecture titled “Democracy and Development: Rethinking the Leadership Question,” organised to commemorate the 59th birthday of Adamawa State Governor, Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri. Osinbajo, who served as vice-president under former President Muhammadu Buhari from 2015 to 2023, expressed concern in his lecture about the failure of democratic governance among citizens across Africa after almost three decades of uninterrupted democratic rule in several countries. Citing Afrobarometer surveys, the former vice-president, who was defeated by President Tinubu during the APC presidential primary ahead of the 2023 general elections, highlighted widespread dissatisfaction with democratic institutions, economic hardship, declining public confidence in government and diminishing youth participation in electoral politics. He noted that although 64 per cent of Africans preferred democracy to other forms of government, only 38 per cent were satisfied with the way democracy was working in their respective countries. Osinbajo also cited findings indicating that 59 per cent of Africans considered their national economies to be in bad shape, while 51 per cent said their economies had deteriorated. He further expressed concern over the rising cost of living, unemployment, inadequate access to healthcare and declining voter turnout, warning that persistent hardship could weaken public confidence in democracy, particularly among young people. In a statement from his Media Office on Wednesday, Jibrin, while responding to the presentation, described Osinbajo’s lecture as thought-provoking and intellectually stimulating but said the gloomy picture painted by the surveys was being addressed and that the gaps were partly attributable to inadequate communication between governments and citizens. item.title: Russia woos African leaders at Moscow summit
item.description: A summit with nearly two dozen African leaders opened in Moscow Wednesday, with the Kremlin describing their countries as “natural allies” against the West. The two-day Russia-Africa summit, the third since 2019, comes as Moscow grapples with heavy Western sanctions over its Ukraine offensive and as it provides security assistance to several African governments. Moscow has courted ties with Africa since the Soviet era, and has long looked to the continent as a counterweight to what it sees as Western domination over international affairs. “We are natural allies in building a multipolar world order,” Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said of the summit, referring to a system where political power is no longer concentrated in the West. Russian President Vladimir Putin meanwhile said that that multipolar world was quickly becoming a reality, in an “irreversible” trend. “The era when the fate of entire continents was determined by a narrow bloc of states is irrevocably gone,” he said as he opened a Russia-Africa economic forum, which gathered thousands of Russian and African business leaders in Moscow hours before the high-level summit began. He told the delegations from 48 African countries, including 22 represented by their leaders, that Russia was “prepared to further expand the geographical reach of our agricultural product shipments”. The pledge came as attacks in the Black Sea linked to the conflict in Ukraine continue to disrupt exports of grain from both Russia and Ukraine. – ‘Neocolonialism’ – Putin also announced that Moscow planned to “localise” the production of “effective Russian medicines and vaccines” on the African continent, and noted that the number of African students in Russia had swelled 50 percent since 2020. The Russian president also stressed that his country was “open to sharing our modern competencies and high-tech digital know-how with our African friends”. Putin’s criticism of what he calls Western “neocolonialism” in Africa has resonated on the continent. That is especially true in the Sahel, where Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso have turned their backs on their former colonial ruler France in favour of closer ties with Moscow. Among the around 20 bilateral meetings Putin was scheduled to have with African leaders in Moscow this week was one with his Malian counterpart Assimi Goita, whose government is using Russian paramilitaries to battle a jihadist offensive. – DRC-Rwanda tensions – Putin was also due to meet with Democratic Republic of Congo President Felix Tshisekedi, who is attending the summit as tensions between his country and neighbouring Rwanda continue to flare. The Rwandan-backed M23 movement has seized swathes of the eastern DRC since taking up arms again in 2021, and, despite a US-brokered truce last December, fighting has continued. item.title: Reps approve ₦100.5bn reimbursement for Yobe airport
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has approved a ₦100.5 billion promissory note programme to reimburse the Yobe State Government for constructing the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport in Damaturu. The approved amount is ₦100,509,017,234.55, following the Federal Government’s decision to take over the newly constructed airport. The approval followed consideration of a report by the House Committee on Aids, Loans and Debt Management on Wednesday. Chairman of the committee, Abubakar Hassan Nalaraba, said during a briefing with journalists at the National Assembly, Abuja, that the committee conducted due diligence and inspected the facility before recommending the reimbursement. He said officials of the Federal Ministries of Aviation and Finance, alongside other relevant agencies, provided technical assessments and documentation on the project. “After due diligence and considerations, and after undertaking comprehensive oversight of the airport, receiving the reports of technical officials at the Ministry of Aviation, Ministry of Finance and the accounting office, we recently considered and approved the reimbursement of the airport to Yobe State Government,” Nalaraba said. He added that the committee found the quality of the airport’s infrastructure and equipment satisfactory, noting that professionals had certified the facilities as meeting the required standards. The committee’s report stated that the Federal Ministry of Aviation inspected the completed airport and confirmed that the quality of work met the standards required for its takeover by the Federal Government. It also found that the Yobe State Government had paid the contractors who executed the project, while the Bureau of Public Procurement certified that due process was followed. According to the report, the committee examined submissions from the state government, the Federal Ministries of Finance and Aviation, the Federal Executive Council and the Bureau of Public Procurement. It also reviewed contract agreements, certificates of completion, evidence of payments to contractors, due-process reviews and the bureau’s certificate of no objection. President Bola Tinubu had requested the National Assembly’s approval for the promissory note programme in a communication read on the floor of the House on October 13, 2026. The request was made pursuant to the Debt Management Office (Establishment) Act, 2003, and the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007, which provide for legislative approval of the programme. Promissory note programmes are used to settle outstanding Federal Government liabilities, including reimbursements to state governments for projects executed on behalf of the Federal Government. item.title: NNPCL to resume oil exploration in Borno
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) has pledged to resume oil exploration activities in Borno State, while assuring the state government of steps to address delays in upgrading the Maiduguri Emergency Power Plant. The commitments were made on Wednesday when Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, received the NNPCL management team, led by the board chairman, Engr. Ahmadu Musa Kida, in Maiduguri. The meeting focused on energy development, the resumption of oil exploration in the state and the delayed completion of the emergency power plant upgrade. Zulum stressed the strategic importance of resuming exploration in the Borno Basin, noting that the state had considerable commercial potential and shared borders with three countries. He expressed optimism that renewed exploration efforts by the national oil company would help unlock the state’s hydrocarbon resources and stimulate economic development. The governor, however, expressed concern over the slow pace of work on the Maiduguri Emergency Power Plant, describing the facility as critical to improving electricity supply in the state. He said the materials required for the plant’s upgrade had been on site for about two years, yet the project remained incomplete. Zulum urged the NNPCL management to intervene and remove the bottlenecks delaying the project, stressing that its completion was important to the socio-economic well-being of residents of Maiduguri and neighbouring communities. Responding, Kida assured the governor of the company’s readiness to fast-track the resumption of exploration activities in the Borno Basin and address the challenges delaying the power plant upgrade. He also commended Zulum for his continued support and efforts to create a conducive environment for investment in the state. The meeting was attended by the Deputy Governor, Umar Usman Kadafur; Secretary to the State Government, Bukar Tijani; Acting Chief of Staff, Dr. Babagana Mallumbe; and other senior government officials. Members of the NNPCL delegation included the Executive Vice President, Upstream, Mr. Udy Ntia, and the Executive Vice President, Gas, Power and New Energy, Mr. Olalekon Ogunleye. item.title: Rivers rally shows Wike’s strength, says APC chieftain
item.description: By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Rivers State, Princewill Dike, has described the turnout at Tuesday’s Rainbow Coalition rally in Port Harcourt as evidence of the political influence and mobilisation capacity of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike. Dike, who spoke at the Yakubu Gowon Stadium, venue of the rally to unveil coalition candidates for the 2027 general elections, attributed the large turnout to Wike’s political organisation, grassroots connections and ability to mobilise supporters. He said the gathering had sent a message to those questioning the level of support enjoyed by President Bola Tinubu in Rivers State. “The massive crowd at the gathering is an indication that the President has substantial political backing in the state, contrary to claims by antagonists of the FCT Minister’s political influence,” he said. The activist expressed satisfaction with the rally, attributing its success to effective planning and the commitment of supporters who turned out to identify with the political movement. He described Wike as a pace-setter, adding that the minister’s political achievements and mobilisation record would be difficult for opponents to surpass. Meanwhile, Wike has announced that the proposed campaign rally of President Tinubu in Port Harcourt on November 7, 2026, will hold at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium. Reacting to the announcement, Dike predicted that the presidential rally would attract a crowd comparable to that witnessed at the Yakubu Gowon Stadium, expressing confidence that the venue would be filled to capacity. He said the turnout at Tuesday’s event had raised expectations for the presidential rally, while urging effective crowd management to prevent overcrowding and ensure public safety. Dike also expressed delight that no casualty was recorded at the coalition rally, thanking God for what he described as the successful and peaceful outcome of the gathering. item.title: Reps to grill INEC over 2027 election readiness, voter registration challenges
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has resolved to invite the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to appear before its committee to provide a comprehensive assessment of its preparedness for the 2027 general elections. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by Mansur Manu Soro and Abdussamad Dasuki, which raised concerns over operational challenges facing the commission, particularly in the ongoing Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise. The motion, initially seeking INEC’s appearance before the House, was amended to require the commission to brief the relevant committee on its readiness for the elections. Under the resolution, INEC is expected to appear before the committee within seven legislative days and provide a detailed status report on its preparations for the 2027 general elections. The lawmakers said the assessment should cover voter registration, Permanent Voter Card (PVC) production and distribution, election logistics, deployment of technology, recruitment and training of personnel, electoral security, risk assessment and funding. They also called for information on budgetary appropriations, funds released, outstanding releases and the implications of any funding gaps for the commission’s preparations. The House expressed concern over reports from CVR centres across the country indicating inadequate registration equipment, limited personnel, network challenges, prolonged waiting times and increased demand from citizens seeking to register or update their voter records. According to the lawmakers, these difficulties could restrict the participation of eligible voters, particularly first-time voters, rural residents, persons with disabilities, students and workers. They warned that failure to address the operational gaps promptly could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and threaten the peaceful conduct of the 2027 elections. The lawmakers noted that the credibility, transparency and acceptability of the elections would depend significantly on INEC’s preparedness in areas such as voter education, logistics, technology deployment, personnel training, security coordination and timely funding. They further observed that the recently concluded Ekiti State governorship election had provided useful lessons on election administration, technology deployment, logistics management and stakeholder engagement that could inform preparations for the 2027 polls. The motion acknowledged INEC’s efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s electoral system but stressed the need for sustained parliamentary oversight to ensure that institutions entrusted with critical national responsibilities were adequately prepared, properly funded and accountable. item.title: Four dead, 13 injured in Lagos truck-bus crash
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Four persons, including a commercial bus driver, have died while 13 others sustained critical injuries in a collision involving a truck and a commercial bus on Alaro City Bridge, inward T-Junction, Epe, Lagos State. The crash occurred on Wednesday morning when the truck rammed into a fully loaded commercial bus while both vehicles were crossing the single-lane bridge, trapping victims in the wreckage, according to eyewitnesses. The General Manager of the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA), Mr Olalekan Bakare-Oki, confirmed that four people died in the incident, while 13 other occupants sustained critical injuries. The truck driver also suffered severe injuries, with both legs reportedly severed, and was trapped in the wreckage. LASTMA operatives, with support from the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), evacuated the deceased to a mortuary, while the Lagos State Ambulance Service (LASAMBUS) transported the injured to the nearest medical facility for emergency treatment. Security personnel from the Epe Police Division also reinforced the rescue operations. Bakare-Oki commiserated with the bereaved families, describing the loss of lives as deeply distressing, and wished the injured victims a speedy recovery. He urged motorists to exercise caution, drive responsibly and comply with traffic regulations, particularly on bridges, narrow carriageways and other road bottlenecks. The LASTMA chief reiterated the agency’s commitment to protecting lives and improving road safety through collaboration with other relevant agencies. He also urged motorists to maintain safe following distances, observe prescribed speed limits and avoid dangerous driving manoeuvres, especially on bridges and constricted roadways where reckless driving could result in fatal crashes. item.title: Ebonyi Assembly approves N150m political billboard fees
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State House of Assembly has approved new levies for political billboards and posters in Abakaliki, fixing the fee for presidential and governorship candidates at N150 million, National Assembly candidates at N20 million and State House of Assembly candidates at N5 million. The House also approved a request by Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru to obtain a N9.673 billion loan from Keystone Bank Limited to meet counterpart funding requirements for the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC). On the billboard fees, the lawmakers unanimously adopted a resolution directing the immediate termination of all existing contracts relating to political billboards and posters within the Abakaliki capital city. They also mandated the Commissioner for Capital City Development to take over the enforcement and collection of all levies relating to political billboards and posters. The resolution followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by the Chairman of the House Committee on Capital City Development and Deputy Chief Whip, Hon. Arinze Lucas Chukwu, who represents Ishielu South Constituency. Moving the motion, Chukwu expressed concern over the indiscriminate pasting of political posters and erection of billboards on public buildings, electric poles, streetlights, bridges and fences across the capital city. He described the practice as environmental pollution that undermined Abakaliki’s appearance and deprived the state of internally generated revenue (IGR). Chukwu said competing claims by different agencies over the collection of billboard levies had created confusion, revenue leakages and double taxation. He argued that existing laws empowered the Commissioner for Capital City Development to regulate outdoor advertising within the capital territory. Under the resolution, any political party, aspirant, group, organisation or individual seeking to erect a billboard or paste posters within the capital city must pay the approved levy into a designated government revenue account and obtain an official receipt before proceeding. The House also resolved that the commissioner should designate approved locations for poster pasting and billboard erection and establish a task force to remove installations erected without proof of payment. Defaulters would be required to pay a penalty of 50 per cent of the original levy, in addition to the applicable fee. The lawmakers further directed the Chairman of the Ebonyi State Internal Revenue Service to terminate all contracts, concessions and arrangements with private consultants or agents for political billboards and posters in the capital city. The agency was also directed to hand over all relevant files, data and authority to the Commissioner for Capital City Development. Seconding the motion, the member representing Ivo Constituency, Hon. item.description: *Garth Wadsworth Dooley: Farewell to an Astute Businessman, Father and Mentor* With deep sorrow, we pay tribute to our beloved Garth Wadsworth Dooley, who passed on to glory on October 9, 2026. An astute businessman, a loving father, and a mentor, he lived a life of purpose, leaving behind cherished memories and a legacy worthy of remembrance. His contributions to his family, business associates, and those he mentored will remain a lasting part of his story. As in-laws, the husband to Remilekun and a father to the children, we remember him with gratitude for the role he played in the lives of those around him. His wisdom, guidance, and dedication to his family and pursuits were qualities that distinguished him. Though his passing leaves a void, we take comfort in the knowledge that his life made a meaningful difference and that his legacy will endure through the people he loved and inspired. We pray that Almighty God, in His mercy, will grant his soul eternal rest and comfort the family he has left behind. May those who mourn find strength in their cherished memories of him and peace in the days ahead. Farewell, Garth Wadsworth Dooley. item.title: Copa del Rey matches postponed following Spain train collision
item.description: The Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) announced on Wednesday the postponement of 24 matches in the first round of the Copa del Rey “as a mark of respect and solidarity” with the victims of a high-speed train collision. “The entire Spanish football family stands united in grief over this tragedy and stands ready to assist the authorities in helping the victims of this devastating accident,” the RFEF said in a statement published on its website. “As a mark of respect and solidarity with all the victims of the tragic train accident that occurred on Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo, the RFEF has decided to suspend the 24 matches in the first round of the Copa del Rey originally scheduled for this afternoon and this evening.” The federation added that it will “provide further details in due course regarding the revised tournament schedule and the final kick-off times for the postponed matches”. The latest provisional figures from the Spanish authorities put the death toll at at least 31, with 80 injured, following the collision of two high-speed trains around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid. item.title: 2027: Kwankwaso joins TikTok, promises daily life content
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, has joined TikTok, promising followers authentic information, latest updates and exclusive content about his daily life as he prepares for the 2027 general election alongside presidential candidate Peter Obi. Kwankwaso announced his arrival on the social media platform in a post on his X handle on Wednesday, urging Nigerians to follow his account and engage with his videos. “I am on TikTok! I encourage you all to follow me there for authentic information, the latest updates, and exclusive contents directly related to my daily life. “Nigeria will be OK. — RMK,” he wrote. In a video attached to the post, the former Kano State governor also welcomed users to his account and encouraged them to follow and share his content. “Hello TikTokers, welcome to our TikTok account. Turn on your notifications, follow us, share our video, thank you, and God bless you,” he said. Kwankwaso’s move comes as the NDC steps up preparations for the 2027 presidential election, in which he is expected to run alongside Obi on the party’s ticket. The two opposition figures formally joined the NDC in May after leaving the African Democratic Congress (ADC), following consultations over their political future and the party’s zoning arrangement. Obi was subsequently ratified as the NDC’s presidential candidate at its national convention on May 30, with Kwankwaso named as his running mate. The ticket brings together Obi’s political support base and Kwankwaso’s Kwankwasiyya movement, which has a strong presence in Kano and other parts of the North. The party recently unveiled its National Campaign Council ahead of the 2027 election, with its National Leader, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, named chairman and Obi appointed co-chairman. Kwankwaso was named co-vice-chairman, while Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim was appointed Director-General of the campaign council. The campaign council is expected to coordinate the party’s nationwide campaign activities and mobilisation ahead of the election. item.title: 2027: ‘We’ll rig those who rig elections,’ Peter Obi talks tough
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has threatened to deal with those who rig elections in Nigeria, declaring that his administration would ensure electoral offenders face jail terms if he wins the 2027 presidential election. Obi spoke on Wednesday at an NDC town hall meeting in Nasarawa State, where he addressed party supporters on electoral integrity and the need to strengthen Nigeria’s electoral system. Responding to a question about election rigging, the former Anambra State governor said the party would not allow electoral manipulation to go unchallenged in the next general election. “You didn’t ask about what we are going to do if people rig election next year. Let me assure you, number one, this coming election, we will rig those who rig it,” Obi said. He added that, if elected president, he would ensure that election rigging became impossible under his watch by strengthening political parties and reforming the electoral process. “And let me assure you number two, if I’m elected the President of Nigeria, nobody will rig election in this country again because the first thing we need to do is to strengthen our parties, strengthen the process,” he said. Obi also called for stricter laws governing eligibility to contest elections, arguing that candidates should be required to demonstrate that they had attended primary and secondary school. “Our laws will be strict. For you to contest election, you must have attended a primary school, you must have attended a secondary school and it will be visible, it will be clear,” he said. He warned that anyone who forged academic certificates or falsely claimed to possess the required qualifications would face imprisonment. “If you didn’t attend any of them or forge your certificate, you go to jail,” Obi said. The NDC candidate extended the warning to officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and others involved in election administration, saying anyone found guilty of rigging elections under his government would be prosecuted. “Any INEC official, anybody who is involved with elections under my watch that rigs elections will go to jail,” he declared. Obi said his proposed approach would be anchored on the rule of law, insisting that no individual, regardless of position, should be exempt from accountability. “Under my watch, Nigeria must be a country that has a law, and both from the number one person to the last person must obey the rule of law,” he said. “Nobody must be above the law; nobody will behave rascally.” He said his political ambition was driven by a desire to change the country and build a system in which electoral rules were respected. “That’s why we are doing what we are doing. We want to change Nigeria. A new Nigeria is possible, and that new Nigeria will be OK,” Obi added. item.title: Five Things To Know Today
item.description: Today’s ‘Five Things’ leads with President Tinubu’s new foreign borrowing request, a six-month transport allowance for federal workers, an updated death toll from the Taraba killings, INEC’s investigation into suspicious photographs in the voters’ register, and the findings of the inquiry into deaths in NSCDC custody. 1. Tinubu seeks approval for $20.5 billion and €1.05 billion in fresh foreign loans President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to approve approximately $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion in external borrowing under the Federal Government’s 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan. The request was presented to the Senate on Tuesday, 27 October. The President says the financing will support infrastructure, power, transport, healthcare, agriculture, education and employment-related projects across the country. Senate President Godswill Akpabio referred the request to the relevant committees, directing them to report within one week. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has urged lawmakers to withhold approval pending greater disclosure of project details. The borrowing has not yet been approved. Why it matters: The proposed borrowing is substantial and could have long-term implications for Nigeria’s debt obligations, public finances and infrastructure investment. Watch: The Senate committee’s findings, project-by-project disclosures, loan terms and the Debt Management Office’s assessment of repayment obligations. 2. Federal Government approves ₦70,000 monthly transport support for workers A conciliation meeting between the FG and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC). X/@LabourMinNG The Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress reached several agreements during Tuesday’s negotiations in Abuja, easing immediate tensions over threatened industrial action. The government approved a ₦70,000 monthly transport intervention for federal public service workers across all grade levels, beginning in November 2026 and lasting six months. It also agreed to pay outstanding peculiar-allowance arrears in three monthly instalments and settle 19 months of outstanding health workers’ allowances over three months, beginning in December. However, the parties did not reach agreement on the effective date for a revised national minimum wage. They agreed to establish a negotiation committee and review implementation after one month. Why it matters: The intervention could provide temporary relief to federal workers facing high transport and living costs. It is not a permanent wage increase. Watch: Publication of payment guidelines, evidence that November disbursements begin as promised, the new wage committee and organised labour’s formal response to unresolved demands. 3. item.title: Violence Mars Gov Radda’s Funtua Campaign Flag-off As Supporters Report Injuries, Property Losses
item.description: Violence erupted along the route to the Tinubu–Dikko campaign flag-off in Funtua Zone on Wednesday, leaving several supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) injured and their property destroyed. The victims, who said they were travelling in the convoy of Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Radda, alleged that they were attacked by groups of angry youths and hoodlums while heading to the campaign venue, where the Governor was scheduled to present his administration’s Building Your Future scorecard. Some of the affected supporters told reporters that mobile phones, clothing and other personal belongings were destroyed during the incident, while several people sustained varying degrees of injuries. According to the victims, the attackers, whom they described as armed with machetes, knives, stones and bottles, assaulted them without provocation. “We were simply on our way to attend the campaign flag-off when we encountered some angry youths who attacked us with stones and bottles. Many people were injured, and our property was destroyed. We cannot afford to replace what we lost,” one of the victims said. The victims appealed to security agencies and relevant authorities to investigate the incident and bring those responsible to justice. Earlier, at the Malumfashi town roundabout linking Bakori Local Government Area, stones were seen scattered across the road, while several vehicles reportedly had their windscreens damaged, suggesting earlier disturbances in the area. Despite the disruption, Governor Radda proceeded with the presentation of his administration’s Building Your Future scorecard, highlighting achievements recorded since assuming office and outlining ongoing projects across key sectors ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The statewide campaign is designed to deepen grassroots engagement by taking the administration’s performance and development agenda directly to communities across the three senatorial zones of Funtua, Daura and Katsina, covering all 34 Local Government Areas and 361 wards. Authorities had not issued an official statement on the reported attack at the time of filing this report. item.title: The Signal: The Parties Are Choosing Sides. Will the Voters Follow?
item.description: Tinubu’s political alliances are expanding, Obi and Kwankwaso are sharpening their challenge, and INEC is under pressure to demonstrate transparency. But as the presidential campaign gathers momentum, Nigeria’s politicians may be discovering that winning endorsements is easier than winning public confidence. There is an interesting contradiction emerging in Nigerian politics. At a time when political parties are supposed to be competing against one another, their leading figures are increasingly finding reasons to work together. In Rivers State, Nyesom Wike is assembling a coalition that crosses party boundaries but supports President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates. In Osun, Governor Ademola Adeleke supports Tinubu’s re-election while insisting that his political organisation will compete against the APC in legislative elections. Meanwhile, Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso have established a joint presidential campaign structure, even as other opposition leaders continue discussing the possibility of a broader alliance. And the Independent National Electoral Commission, caught in the middle of growing political suspicion, has taken a step towards addressing concerns about the voters’ register. Welcome to Nigeria’s 2027 election. A contest in which party labels are becoming increasingly flexible, political loyalties are being renegotiated, and the electorate is being asked to distinguish between genuine conviction and political convenience. But beneath the manoeuvring lies a question that could determine the outcome. The politicians are choosing sides. Will the voters follow them? Wike’s coalition: when political boundaries become optional Nyesom Wike has never been a politician easily constrained by conventional party loyalties. His support for Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, despite his association with the PDP, demonstrated his willingness to pursue political objectives across party lines. Now, with another presidential election approaching, he is taking that approach further. At a political gathering in Eleme, Rivers State, Wike made it clear that his Rainbow Coalition is not simply an arrangement to support Tinubu’s re-election. It also intends to support APC candidates contesting governorship and legislative elections. That is a significant development. It suggests that Wike is attempting to create a political structure capable of influencing elections at several levels, regardless of the formal party affiliations of those participating. There is a certain political logic to the arrangement. For Tinubu, Wike provides an influential ally in a strategically important state. For Wike, cooperation with the President offers a means of preserving political relevance and strengthening his position in Rivers. But what does the arrangement offer ordinary voters?
